applicationInfo.name: Financial Health - AI-Powered Debt Optimization Platform
applicationInfo.description:
### Summary
Financial Health is a multi-agent AI financial assistant that analyzes credit card statements, diagnoses financial health, detects recurring expenses, and generates optimized debt repayment plans with interactive visualizations. Built with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK.

### Key objectives
- Extract structured data from credit card statements across multiple financial institutions
- Diagnose user financial health and generate optimized debt repayment strategies
- Detect recurring small expenses that impact debt capacity
- Provide month-over-month financial evolution tracking with persistent memory
- Enable scenario simulation for financial decision-making

### Use-cases
- Users upload PDF credit card statements from multiple banks and retailers
- System extracts data using Claude Vision, stores in DynamoDB, and analyzes debt composition
- Generates personalized repayment plans using avalanche or snowball methods
- Identifies recurring expenses by category and quantifies potential savings
- Users simulate scenarios like bonuses, expense cuts, or new purchases
- Monthly follow-up compares current vs previous analysis to show progress

### Features
- Multi-agent orchestration with specialized agents for extraction, analysis, detection, and simulation
- PDF document processing with Claude Sonnet 4.5 Vision for multi-format bank statements
- Parallel execution of analysis and detection agents for performance
- AgentCore Memory for session persistence and user preference tracking
- Bedrock Guardrails for content filtering and PII anonymization
- Interactive charts for debt composition, evolution, interest comparison, spending breakdown, and alternatives
- Multi-country support with currency and terminology adaptation
- Cognito authentication with custom user attributes for financial profile
- Real-time job polling for async agent processing
- S3 presigned URLs for secure document uploads
- CloudFront CDN distribution for frontend
- Financial history tracking in DynamoDB with temporal snapshots

architecture.description:
### High Level Architecture

#### Application type
Serverless multi-agent AI web application for financial debt analysis and optimization

#### Layers
- Presentation: React SPA with AWS Amplify authentication
- API: API Gateway with Cognito authorizer, Lambda functions
- Agent orchestration: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime with multi-agent coordination
- Data: DynamoDB tables, S3 buckets for documents and static assets
- AI/ML: Amazon Bedrock foundation models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5)

#### Boundaries
- External: Users via CloudFront CDN
- API boundary: API Gateway with JWT authentication
- Agent boundary: AgentCore Runtime with isolated microVMs per session
- Data boundary: DynamoDB and S3 with IAM-based access control
- AI boundary: Bedrock Guardrails for content filtering and PII anonymization

#### Technology components
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, AWS Amplify, Recharts, Vite
- Backend: Python 3.13, Strands Agents SDK, Bedrock AgentCore SDK, Boto3
- Infrastructure: AWS CDK (Python), CloudFormation
- AI Models: Claude Sonnet 4.5 (orchestrator, extractor), Claude Haiku 4.5 (workers)
- Storage: DynamoDB (NoSQL), S3 (object storage)
- Auth: Amazon Cognito User Pools

#### Deployment architecture
- CloudFront distribution with S3 origin for frontend static assets
- API Gateway REST API with Lambda proxy integrations
- Lambda functions: dispatcher, async worker, polling, presigned URLs, history queries
- AgentCore Runtime: serverless microVM execution environment
- DynamoDB tables: estados_cuenta, file_hashes, jobs, financial_history
- S3 buckets: frontend assets, PDF documents

#### APIs
| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|----------|
| /invoke | POST | Dispatch agent job, returns job_id |
| /job/{job_id} | GET | Poll job status and results |
| /upload | POST | Generate presigned URL for PDF upload |
| /history/{usuario_id} | GET | Retrieve financial history snapshots |
| /last-analysis/{usuario_id} | GET | Get most recent completed analysis |
| /user-documents/{usuario_id} | GET | List user uploaded documents |
| /documents/{usuario_id}/{file_hash} | DELETE | Delete document and associated data |

#### Security relevant components
- Cognito User Pools: email-based authentication, custom attributes for profile
- Bedrock Guardrails: content filtering (violence, sexual, hate, insults), PII anonymization
- API Gateway Authorizer: JWT validation on all endpoints except OPTIONS
- S3 presigned URLs: time-limited (15min) upload/download access
- IAM roles: least-privilege for Lambda, AgentCore Runtime
- KMS key: encryption for AgentCore Memory
- DynamoDB encryption: AWS-managed keys with point-in-time recovery

### Low Level Architecture

- CloudFront CDN: serves React SPA, OAC for S3 origin, security headers policy
- API Gateway: REST API with CORS, Cognito authorizer, Lambda integrations
- Lambda dispatcher: receives requests, creates job in DynamoDB, invokes worker async
- Lambda worker: executes AgentCore Runtime with timeout protection, saves results
- AgentCore Runtime: hosts multi-agent orchestrator with isolated microVM per session
- Orchestrator agent: Claude Sonnet 4.5 with Guardrails, coordinates sub-agents
- Extractor agent: Claude Sonnet 4.5 Vision, parallel PDF processing
- Analyst agent: Claude Haiku 4.5, financial health diagnosis, payment plans
- Detective agent: Claude Haiku 4.5, recurring expense detection
- Simulator agent: Claude Haiku 4.5, scenario simulation
- AgentCore Memory: three strategies (preferences, facts, summaries), KMS encrypted
- DynamoDB estados_cuenta: PK usuario_id, SK tarjeta_id, stores card statements
- DynamoDB file_hashes: PK usuario_id, SK file_hash, deduplication control
- DynamoDB jobs: PK job_id, GSI usuario_id-completed_at-index for history
- DynamoDB financial_history: PK usuario_id, SK timestamp, KPI snapshots
- S3 pdfs_bucket: temporary storage for uploaded statements, presigned URL access
- S3 frontend_bucket: static assets, CloudFront origin
- Cognito User Pool: email sign-in, custom attributes (country, currency, income, language, payment_behavior)
- SSM Parameter Store: runtime configuration for AgentCore
- Python tools: financial calculations, DynamoDB persistence, parallel execution

dataflow.description:
### Human actors
- End User: Uploads credit card statements, views analysis, simulates scenarios
- System Administrator: Manages infrastructure, monitors logs
- Unauthenticated Visitor: Accesses login page only

### External entities
- Amazon Bedrock: Claude AI models (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5) for vision and text
- Amazon Cognito: User authentication and JWT token issuance
- AWS CloudWatch: Logging and monitoring aggregation

### Processes
- React SPA: Frontend UI, handles file upload, chart rendering, chat interface
- API Gateway: REST API with Cognito authorizer, routes requests to Lambda
- Lambda Dispatcher: Creates async jobs, invokes worker Lambda
- Lambda Worker: Executes AgentCore Runtime, processes multi-agent workflows
- AgentCore Runtime: Orchestrates 5 specialized AI agents with microVM isolation
- Lambda Presigned URL Generator: Creates time-limited S3 upload URLs
- Lambda Job Poller: Returns job status and results to frontend

### Data stores

| Store | Type | High-Value (Y/N) |
|-------|------|------------------|
| DynamoDB estados_cuenta | NoSQL table | Y - PII, financial data, transactions |
| DynamoDB jobs | NoSQL table | Y - Analysis results, session IDs |
| DynamoDB file_hashes | NoSQL table | N - Deduplication metadata |
| DynamoDB financial_history | NoSQL table | Y - Temporal KPI snapshots |
| S3 pdfs_bucket | Object storage | Y - Credit card statements (PDFs) |
| S3 frontend_bucket | Object storage | N - Static web assets |
| AgentCore Memory | KMS-encrypted memory | Y - User preferences, conversation history |

### Trust boundaries

| Zone | Elements | Trust Level |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Public Internet | CloudFront, unauthenticated users | Untrusted |
| Authenticated Web | React SPA with valid JWT | Low trust |
| API Layer | API Gateway with Cognito authorizer | Medium trust |
| Backend Services | Lambda functions with IAM roles | High trust |
| AI Processing | AgentCore Runtime with microVM isolation | High trust |

### Data flows

| Flow ID | Description | Source | Target | Trust Boundaries Crossed | Assets |
|---------|-------------|--------|--------|--------------------------|--------|
| DF-01 | User login request | React SPA | Cognito | Public to API | Email, password |
| DF-02 | JWT token response | Cognito | React SPA | API to Public | JWT token with user claims |
| DF-03 | Request presigned URL | React SPA | Lambda Presigned URL | Authenticated Web to Backend | JWT, filename, file hash |
| DF-04 | Presigned URL response | Lambda Presigned URL | React SPA | Backend to Authenticated Web | Time-limited S3 upload URL |
| DF-05 | PDF upload to S3 | React SPA | S3 pdfs_bucket | Authenticated Web to Backend | Credit card statement PDF |
| DF-06 | Dispatch analysis job | React SPA | Lambda Dispatcher | Authenticated Web to Backend | JWT, prompt, S3 URIs, session_id |
| DF-07 | Create job record | Lambda Dispatcher | DynamoDB jobs | Backend to Backend | job_id, usuario_id, status |
| DF-08 | Async worker invocation | Lambda Dispatcher | Lambda Worker | Backend to Backend | job_id, prompt, usuario_id |
| DF-09 | Invoke AgentCore Runtime | Lambda Worker | AgentCore Runtime | Backend to AI Processing | Payload with prompt, usuario_id |
| DF-10 | Download PDF from S3 | AgentCore Runtime | S3 pdfs_bucket | AI Processing to Backend | S3 URI |
| DF-11 | Extract data with Claude Vision | AgentCore Runtime | Bedrock | AI Processing to External | PDF as base64, extraction prompt |
| DF-12 | Vision extraction response | Bedrock | AgentCore Runtime | External to AI Processing | Structured JSON with card data |
| DF-13 | Persist extracted data | AgentCore Runtime | DynamoDB estados_cuenta | AI Processing to Backend | Card details, transactions |
| DF-14 | Financial analysis request | AgentCore Runtime | Bedrock | AI Processing to External | Card data, analysis prompt |
| DF-15 | Analysis response | Bedrock | AgentCore Runtime | External to AI Processing | Debt strategy, KPIs, charts |
| DF-16 | Store job result | Lambda Worker | DynamoDB jobs | Backend to Backend | Analysis result, charts, session_id |
| DF-17 | Save financial snapshot | Lambda Worker | DynamoDB financial_history | Backend to Backend | KPIs, fecha_corte, timestamp |
| DF-18 | Poll job status | React SPA | Lambda Job Poller | Authenticated Web to Backend | JWT, job_id |
| DF-19 | Job status response | Lambda Job Poller | React SPA | Backend to Authenticated Web | Status, result, charts |
| DF-20 | Chat message submission | React SPA | Lambda Dispatcher | Authenticated Web to Backend | JWT, prompt, session_id |
| DF-21 | Query user cards | AgentCore Runtime | DynamoDB estados_cuenta | AI Processing to Backend | usuario_id |
| DF-22 | Load previous analysis | Lambda Worker | DynamoDB jobs | Backend to Backend | usuario_id, GSI query |
| DF-23 | Memory retrieval | AgentCore Runtime | AgentCore Memory | AI Processing to AI Processing | session_id, actor_id |
| DF-24 | Memory persistence | AgentCore Runtime | AgentCore Memory | AI Processing to AI Processing | Preferences, facts, summaries |
| DF-25 | Delete document request | React SPA | Lambda Delete Document | Authenticated Web to Backend | JWT, usuario_id, file_hash |
| DF-26 | Delete from S3 | Lambda Delete Document | S3 pdfs_bucket | Backend to Backend | S3 key |
| DF-27 | Delete from DynamoDB | Lambda Delete Document | DynamoDB tables | Backend to Backend | usuario_id, tarjeta_id, file_hash |
| DF-28 | Financial history query | React SPA | Lambda History | Authenticated Web to Backend | JWT, usuario_id |
| DF-29 | History response | Lambda History | React SPA | Backend to Authenticated Web | Temporal KPI snapshots |
| DF-30 | Guardrail filtering | AgentCore Runtime | Bedrock Guardrails | AI Processing to External | User prompt, model response |
| DF-31 | PII anonymization | Bedrock Guardrails | AgentCore Runtime | External to AI Processing | Filtered/anonymized content |

mitigations.content: Implement short-lived JWT access tokens (15 minutes) with secure refresh token rotation. Configure Cognito User Pool with appropriate token expiration settings and enable token revocation lists for compromised tokens.

metadata.value: Short token lifetimes limit the exposure window if tokens are stolen. Refresh token rotation ensures that even if a refresh token is compromised, it becomes invalid after use. Cognito supports these configurations natively through User Pool settings. Consider implementing token binding to prevent token theft via XSS or network interception.

mitigations.content: Implement API Gateway usage plans with per-user rate limiting (e.g., 10 requests per minute for analysis endpoints, 100 for polling). Use Cognito user ID as the throttling key to prevent individual users from exhausting system resources.

metadata.value: API Gateway usage plans provide built-in throttling without additional infrastructure. Rate limits should be tuned based on legitimate usage patterns (typical session takes 370 seconds with 5 agent cycles). Consider implementing burst allowances for legitimate spikes while preventing sustained abuse. Monitor CloudWatch metrics for throttled requests to tune limits.

mitigations.content: Add Lambda authorization layer that validates resource ownership before processing. For all data access operations, verify that the usuario_id from JWT claims matches the owner of the requested resource (job_id, file_hash, session_id) by querying DynamoDB before proceeding.

metadata.value: API Gateway validates JWT authenticity but not resource-level authorization. Implement a reusable authorization function that queries DynamoDB to verify ownership before allowing access to jobs, documents, or sessions. This prevents horizontal privilege escalation where authenticated users access other users' data. Consider caching authorization decisions for frequently accessed resources to minimize DynamoDB reads.

mitigations.content: Implement S3 bucket policies that restrict presigned URL access to specific IP ranges or require additional request headers. Add server-side validation that presigned URLs can only access objects matching the authenticated user's usuario_id prefix in the S3 key structure.

metadata.value: While presigned URLs expire in 15 minutes, additional restrictions reduce risk if URLs are intercepted. Structure S3 keys as usuario_id/file_hash/filename.pdf and validate that presigned URLs can only access paths matching the authenticated user. Consider using S3 Object Lambda to validate access at runtime. For high-security deployments, implement VPC endpoints for S3 access to prevent internet exposure.

mitigations.content: Deploy CloudWatch Log Insights queries and EventBridge rules to detect anomalous patterns: multiple failed authentication attempts, rapid job creation, unusual data access patterns, or attempts to access resources across different usuario_ids. Configure SNS alerts for security team notification.

metadata.value: Detective controls identify attacks in progress. Create CloudWatch dashboards showing authentication failures, authorization denials, rate limit hits, and cross-user access attempts. Use CloudWatch Anomaly Detection for baseline establishment and automatic alerting. Consider integrating with AWS Security Hub for centralized security monitoring. Log all authorization decisions (success and failure) for forensic analysis.

mitigations.content: Implement comprehensive input validation for PDF uploads: file size limits (e.g., 10MB max), MIME type verification, and PDF structure validation using a library like PyPDF2 before passing to Claude Vision. Reject files with embedded JavaScript, forms, or suspicious metadata.

metadata.value: Malicious PDFs can exploit parsing vulnerabilities or contain embedded threats. Validate file size to prevent resource exhaustion, verify MIME type matches file extension, and use PDF parsing libraries to detect malformed or malicious structures. Consider implementing antivirus scanning using AWS Lambda integration with ClamAV or third-party services. Sanitize PDF metadata before processing to remove potential exploit vectors.

mitigations.content: Enhance Bedrock Guardrails configuration with custom word filters and contextual grounding to detect prompt injection attempts. Implement additional validation layer in Lambda that checks for suspicious patterns (e.g., ignore previous instructions, system prompts, role-play attempts) before passing prompts to AgentCore Runtime.

metadata.value: Bedrock Guardrails provide baseline protection but can be bypassed with sophisticated techniques. Implement pre-processing that detects common prompt injection patterns using regex or ML-based classification. Consider using prompt templates that clearly separate user input from system instructions. Log all prompts flagged as suspicious for security review. Apply guardrails to sub-agents in addition to orchestrator for defense-in-depth.

mitigations.content: Implement DynamoDB conditional writes for critical operations including file deduplication hash insertion, job state transitions, and concurrent agent writes. Use attribute_not_exists() conditions for hash table inserts and version numbers for optimistic locking on updates.

metadata.value: DynamoDB conditional writes provide atomic operations preventing race conditions. For file_hashes table, use conditional put with attribute_not_exists(file_hash) to ensure only one upload succeeds. For job state transitions, add a version attribute and increment on each update with condition checking previous version. This prevents race conditions in parallel agent execution and timeout protection mechanisms.

mitigations.content: Configure CloudWatch Logs with sensitive data filtering to automatically redact credit card numbers, account numbers, and PII before log persistence. Implement structured logging with explicit field marking for sensitive data and use AWS Lambda Powertools Logger with custom formatters.

metadata.value: CloudWatch Logs data protection can automatically mask sensitive patterns using regex. Configure patterns for credit card numbers, account numbers, emails, and phone numbers. Use structured JSON logging to clearly identify sensitive fields and apply redaction consistently. Set appropriate log retention periods (e.g., 30 days for application logs, 90 days for security logs) and restrict IAM access to logs containing financial data.

mitigations.content: Implement IAM role session tags and attribute-based access control (ABAC) for Lambda functions. Tag resources with usuario_id and configure IAM policies that only allow access to resources with matching tags. Enable AWS CloudTrail for comprehensive audit logging of all IAM and data access operations.

metadata.value: ABAC provides fine-grained access control at the IAM level, complementing application-layer authorization. Tag DynamoDB items and S3 objects with usuario_id and configure Lambda execution role policies to only access resources with matching tags. CloudTrail provides immutable audit logs for forensic analysis and compliance. Enable CloudTrail Insights to detect unusual API activity patterns indicating compromised credentials.

mitigations.content: Implement cryptographically secure session_id generation using Python's secrets module with at least 32 bytes of entropy. Bind session_id to usuario_id in AgentCore Memory configuration and validate binding on every memory access operation to prevent session hijacking.

metadata.value: Use secrets.token_urlsafe(32) to generate unpredictable session IDs. Store session_id to usuario_id mapping in DynamoDB with TTL for automatic cleanup. Validate that session_id belongs to the authenticated user before any AgentCore Memory operation. Consider implementing session invalidation on logout and automatic expiration after inactivity period. Monitor for session enumeration attempts.

mitigations.content: Implement output validation and sanitization for all LLM-generated content before storage and rendering. Use JSON schema validation for chart data, HTML sanitization libraries (e.g., bleach) for text content, and Content Security Policy headers in CloudFront to prevent XSS attacks.

metadata.value: LLM outputs can contain malicious content if prompt injection succeeds. Validate chart JSON against strict schemas before extraction and rendering. Use bleach or similar libraries to sanitize any HTML content. Configure CloudFront to add Content-Security-Policy headers restricting script sources to same-origin only. React's built-in XSS protection helps but explicit validation provides defense-in-depth.

mitigations.content: Migrate from CORS allow-all to explicit CloudFront domain allowlist after stack creation. Implement CSRF token validation for state-changing operations (job dispatch, document deletion) using double-submit cookie pattern or synchronizer tokens.

metadata.value: Update CORS configuration post-deployment to only allow the CloudFront distribution domain. For CSRF protection, generate random tokens server-side and validate on state-changing requests. Store CSRF tokens in secure, httpOnly cookies and require matching token in request headers. This prevents malicious sites from making authenticated requests even with valid JWT.

mitigations.content: Enable AWS Config rules to continuously monitor IAM role permissions, S3 bucket policies, and DynamoDB encryption settings. Configure automatic remediation for policy violations and alert on any privilege escalation or overly permissive configurations.

metadata.value: AWS Config provides continuous compliance monitoring. Enable rules like iam-policy-no-statements-with-admin-access, s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, and dynamodb-table-encrypted-kms. Configure automatic remediation using AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to revert unauthorized changes. Integrate with AWS Security Hub for centralized security posture management.

mitigations.content: Implement Lambda function timeout protection with graceful shutdown: use threading.Event for cancellation signaling, mark jobs as FAILED with detailed error messages before timeout, and implement idempotency tokens to prevent duplicate processing if function is retried.

metadata.value: Current timeout protection uses ThreadPoolExecutor but could have race conditions. Implement cooperative cancellation using threading.Event that worker thread checks periodically. Update job status to FAILED with timestamp and reason before Lambda terminates. Add idempotency_token to job records and check on worker start to prevent duplicate processing if dispatcher retries. Log timeout events for capacity planning.

mitigations.content: Implement DynamoDB Streams with Lambda trigger to create immutable audit trail of all data modifications. Store audit events in separate append-only table with WORM (Write Once Read Many) characteristics for forensic analysis and compliance.

metadata.value: DynamoDB Streams capture all item-level changes. Create Lambda function that processes stream events and writes to audit table with fields: timestamp, usuario_id, table_name, operation, old_values, new_values, request_id. Configure audit table with point-in-time recovery and longer retention than operational tables. This provides tamper-evident audit trail for investigating data integrity issues.

mitigations.content: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) in Cognito User Pool for all users. Configure adaptive authentication to require additional verification for high-risk operations like document deletion or when access patterns deviate from normal behavior.

metadata.value: Cognito supports MFA via SMS, TOTP, or authenticator apps. Enable MFA for all users to prevent account takeover from password compromise. Configure advanced security features including adaptive authentication that analyzes device, location, and behavior patterns. Require step-up authentication for sensitive operations. Consider risk-based authentication that challenges users only when suspicious activity is detected.

mitigations.content: Implement data integrity verification for stored financial data using HMAC signatures. Calculate HMAC-SHA256 of critical fields (balances, interest rates, transaction amounts) using KMS-managed keys and verify signatures before using data for calculations or analysis.

metadata.value: Protect against tampering of stored financial data by adding integrity signatures. Use AWS KMS to generate HMAC keys and calculate signatures on write operations. Store signatures alongside data in DynamoDB. Verify signatures before reading data for analysis. This detects unauthorized modifications even if attacker has DynamoDB write access. Consider implementing versioning with signatures to track all changes.

mitigations.content: Deploy AWS WAF on API Gateway with managed rule groups for common attack patterns (SQL injection, XSS, known bad inputs). Configure custom rules to block requests with suspicious patterns in prompts, enforce request size limits, and implement geo-blocking if appropriate.

metadata.value: AWS WAF provides layer 7 protection before requests reach Lambda. Enable AWS Managed Rules including Core Rule Set, Known Bad Inputs, and SQL Database protection. Create custom rules to detect prompt injection patterns, limit request body size to prevent resource exhaustion, and block requests from high-risk countries if user base is geographically concentrated. Monitor WAF metrics and tune rules to minimize false positives.

mitigations.content: Implement Lambda reserved concurrency limits for worker functions to prevent resource exhaustion. Set limits based on Bedrock API quotas and desired cost controls (e.g., 10 concurrent executions). Configure SQS dead-letter queues for failed invocations to enable retry and investigation.

metadata.value: Reserved concurrency prevents runaway resource consumption and ensures predictable costs. Calculate appropriate limits based on Bedrock quotas (requests per minute) and Lambda account limits. Use SQS as event source for worker Lambda instead of async invocation to gain better control over retry behavior and visibility into failed jobs. Configure dead-letter queue with appropriate retention for forensic analysis of failures.

mitigations.content: Implement comprehensive security testing including SAST (Static Application Security Testing) for code vulnerabilities, DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) for runtime issues, and regular penetration testing focused on AI-specific attack vectors like prompt injection and model manipulation.

metadata.value: Integrate security testing into CI/CD pipeline. Use tools like Bandit for Python SAST to detect common vulnerabilities. Implement DAST using OWASP ZAP or similar tools to test deployed application. Conduct regular penetration testing with focus on AI-specific threats: prompt injection, model inversion, data poisoning, and adversarial inputs. Maintain vulnerability management program to track and remediate findings.

mitigations.content: Implement request signing and validation for AgentCore Runtime invocations. Use AWS SigV4 signing with request timestamp validation (reject requests older than 5 minutes) and nonce tracking to prevent replay attacks. Log all invocation attempts with caller identity for audit.

metadata.value: Current implementation has SDK fallback to manual HTTP with SigV4. Strengthen this by implementing strict timestamp validation to prevent replay attacks. Maintain short-term cache of request signatures or nonces to detect duplicates. Validate that IAM principal making request has appropriate permissions for the specific agent and session. Log all invocation attempts including denied requests for security monitoring.

mitigations.content: Implement soft delete pattern for document deletion operations. Mark documents as deleted with timestamp and usuario_id but retain data for configurable retention period (e.g., 30 days). Require additional confirmation for permanent deletion and log all deletion operations.

metadata.value: Soft deletes provide recovery capability and audit trail. Add deleted_at timestamp field to DynamoDB items and filter deleted items from normal queries. Implement scheduled Lambda function to permanently delete items after retention period. Require additional authentication (e.g., email confirmation code) for permanent deletion. This protects against accidental deletion and provides forensic evidence if deletion was unauthorized.

mitigations.content: Implement context isolation for previous analysis injection. Validate and sanitize historical data before including in prompts. Use separate memory namespaces per usuario_id in AgentCore Memory and verify namespace isolation. Add integrity checks to detect tampering of historical job results.

metadata.value: Previous analysis context could be attack vector if tampered. Before injecting historical data into prompts, validate structure and content against expected schemas. Sanitize any user-controlled fields to prevent prompt injection via historical data. Implement HMAC signatures on job results to detect tampering. Verify AgentCore Memory namespaces are properly isolated per user to prevent cross-user context leakage.

mitigations.content: Implement JSON schema validation for all chart data extraction using jsonschema library. Validate structure, data types, and value ranges before storage and rendering. Implement timeout protection for regex operations to prevent ReDoS attacks during KPI extraction.

metadata.value: Chart data extraction uses regex which could be vulnerable to ReDoS. Define strict JSON schemas for each chart type and validate LLM outputs before regex extraction. Use re2 library instead of standard re for regex operations to prevent catastrophic backtracking. Implement timeouts on regex operations. Validate extracted KPI values are within reasonable ranges before storing in financial_history table.
